facts.fact: Minister Zerrouki told the APN that Algeria is connected to the global internet through four submarine cable systems, SEA-ME-WE 4, Medex, Orval (Oran-Valence) and Alval (Alger-Valence), plus an Alger-Palma cable; the document names Oran and Algiers as separate cable origins but does not use the words landing station.

note: Medusa (service due early 2028) and the Medex extension (works to June 2026) are not yet in service; international capacity above 10.2 Tbit/s is bandwidth only and is not a fact.
Project launch of the Medusa cable from the Port of Algiers; not in service, so no route fact.

facts.fact: The Ministry of Post and Telecommunications said maintenance on the Algeria-Spain submarine cable was completed overnight 26-27 October 2026 and internet service returned to normal.
The ministry said data traffic was switched beforehand to other submarine cables, so main internet services were not affected during the works.

note: Cables not named; landing stations not stated, so independence is not shown.

facts.fact: Algerie Telecom's CEO says its subsidiary Algerie Telecom Europe manages the submarine cables linking Algeria to the major data backbones in Europe and the global network.

note: Capacity sale to neighbours is stated as an ambition only; landing stations and independence of routes not given.

facts.fact: Algérie Télécom says its network links Algeria abroad through the SeaMeWe4, MEDEX, ORVAL/ALVAL and MAREA submarine cables and through land cables to neighbouring countries such as Tunisia.
